question: How many skills before coverage saturates, and does findability degrade first?
answer: Findability does not degrade first. It degrades ALWAYS. The library is worth nothing until the right skill can be found, and finding is the bottleneck -- not learning.

what_this_does_to_the_thesis.the_claim: learn a thing once and it is permanently available
what_this_does_to_the_thesis.the_measurement: it is permanently STORED; availability is a separate, unsolved problem that gets WORSE as the library grows
what_this_does_to_the_thesis.so: 'instant learning' solves the cheap half. The expensive half -- finding the learned thing among the others -- is where the library dies, and adding skills makes it worse. A library of 100 is 9x less precise than a library of 5.
what_this_does_to_the_thesis.and: r52 in this repo measured the same effect from the other side: teaching more near-duplicates made selection worse

the_smart_response_measured_partly.hierarchical_routing: the literature's answer; NOT built here

the_smart_response_measured_partly.what_was_built: a mechanical router that reports its own doubt, plus a model that is called ONLY where the router refuses -- 3/10 free, 10/10 with 7 model calls
the_smart_response_measured_partly.why_that_matters: it turns retrieval into a cost curve instead of a cliff, and it keeps the model out of the 30% of cases that never needed it

what_this_does_not_prove: that my 10/10 generalises: ten hand-routed sentences by one model is not a benchmark
